This document demonstrates quarto-term rendering to multiple output formats from the same source.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
Download this document in other formats: [PDF](demo-formats.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm} [EPUB](demo-formats.epub){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm} [Markdown](demo-formats.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm}
:::

## Basic output

```{term}
echo "Hello from quarto-term"
```

## State persistence

Variables carry over between cells:

```{term}
export NAME="world"
```

```{term}
echo "Hello, $NAME"
```

## Multi-line commands

```{term}
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  echo "Item $i"
done
```

## ANSI colors

Full color support across all formats:

```{term}
printf '\033[31mred\033[0m \033[32mgreen\033[0m \033[34mblue\033[0m \033[33myellow\033[0m\n'
```

```{term}
for i ({0..15}) { print -nP "%K{$i} ${(l:2:)i} %k"; ((i%8==7))&&print }
```

## Working with files

```{term}
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/demo.txt
name,value
alpha,1
beta,2
gamma,3
EOF
cat /tmp/demo.txt
```

## Piping

```{term}
seq 1 10 | paste -sd+ | bc
```

## Interactive commands

```{term}
sleep 100 #! expect-prompt: false
ctrl-c #! literal: false, delay: 0.5, expect-prompt: true
echo 'Back to the prompt!'
```

## Per-cell styling
```{term}
#| style.colorscheme: nord
echo "This cell uses a different colorscheme"
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f /tmp/demo.txt
```
